problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis and its velocity at time $t\ge 0$ is given by $v(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+\frac{\pi }{6}).$ At time $t=0$ the particle is located at the position $x=1.$ What is the position of the particle at time $t=\frac{\pi }{3}?$
worked_solution:
The position of the particle at $t=\frac{\pi }{3}$ is equal to its position at $t=0$ plus the total displacement over $t\in [0,\frac{\pi }{3}].$ Therefore, we can calculate it as follows:

$$
x(\frac{\pi }{3})=x(0)+{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}v(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

Carrying out the computations, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x(\frac{\pi }{3}) & =1+{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+\frac{\pi }{6})\,\text{d}t \\  & =1+{[-\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+\frac{\pi }{6})]}_{0}^{\pi /3} \\  & =1+([-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}+\frac{\pi }{6})]-[-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0+\frac{\pi }{6})]) \\  & =1+(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})) \\  & =1+(-0+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =1+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}+2}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So the position of the particle at $t=\frac{\pi }{3}$ is $x=\frac{\sqrt{3}+2}{2}.$
